instrucciones: Answer all five questions in ENGLISH. Read the text in Question 1 carefully; it is also the text for Questions 2 and 3. Question 1: answer all four items. Question 2: answer TWO of the three questions. Question 3: choose THREE of the four items. Question 4: answer all the items. Question 5: choose ONE of the two options and write 140–160 words. If you answer more options than required, only the first ones will be corrected. No dictionary or other educational resource may be used for Questions 1–3. Maximum score: 10 points.

preguntas.enunciado:
Read the text and answer all the questions below.

FIX-IT SATURDAYS: A COMMUNITY LEARNS TO REPAIR

The project began in March 2025, when residents of Llucmajor started meeting once a month to repair household objects instead of throwing them away. Fix-It Saturdays now take place on the second Saturday of each month. People bring items such as lamps, small kitchen appliances and toys to a volunteer team that includes retired technicians and local students.

At first, the sessions were held in an upstairs room at the public library. After two wheelchair users could not reach the room, the organisers moved the project in July to a ground-floor room at the civic centre. The new space is easier to enter and has enough tables for separate repair stations.

There is no fixed fee for a repair; a jar accepts voluntary donations, which help pay for replacement parts. A nearby hardware shop also provides surplus screws and switches that are still safe to use. When an item arrives, volunteers record its condition and carry out a basic safety check. Only trained adults handle appliances connected to mains electricity. Students never open electrical devices unless a qualified adult is working beside them.

The students have other useful jobs. They welcome visitors, log each item and, with the owner’s permission, take photographs of the repair process. They then help prepare short guides explaining simple fixes. Organisers say this helps visitors understand how an object works, even if it cannot be repaired. Items that are beyond repair are safely recycled, while useful parts are salvaged for future projects.

By its tenth month, the team had recorded 146 objects: 101 were repaired, while the other 45 were safely recycled or kept for parts. The organisers do not describe the project as a shop or a professional repair service. They see it as a place where neighbours can share skills, reduce waste and feel more confident about trying a simple repair at home.

A) Indicate whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE. Justify your answer by quoting directly from the text. No marks will be awarded for answers that only state TRUE or FALSE. Do not use ellipses. (0.5 points each)

a) Fix-It Saturdays began in March 2025.
b) Visitors must pay a fixed fee for every repair.
c) Students may open electrical devices without an adult supervising them.
d) In the project’s first ten months, 101 of the 146 recorded objects were repaired.
preguntas.solucion:
### Resolución paso a paso

Como es un ejercicio de comprensión lectora, contrasto cada afirmación con la información explícita del texto y la justifico con una cita literal completa.

**a) TRUE.** El texto indica: “The project began in March 2025, when residents of Llucmajor started meeting once a month to repair household objects instead of throwing them away.” La fecha coincide con la afirmación.

**b) FALSE.** El texto dice: “There is no fixed fee for a repair; a jar accepts voluntary donations, which help pay for replacement parts.” Por tanto, no hay una tarifa fija obligatoria; las donaciones son voluntarias.

**c) FALSE.** El texto afirma: “Students never open electrical devices unless a qualified adult is working beside them.” Así pues, los estudiantes no pueden abrir esos aparatos sin la supervisión de un adulto cualificado.

**d) TRUE.** El texto dice: “By its tenth month, the team had recorded 146 objects: 101 were repaired, while the other 45 were safely recycled or kept for parts.” Coinciden tanto el total de objetos como los 101 reparados.

**Comprobación final:** las respuestas son TRUE, FALSE, FALSE y TRUE. Son cuatro apartados de 0,5 puntos, por lo que la puntuación máxima es $4 \times 0{,}5 = 2$ puntos.
preguntas.resultado: a) TRUE; b) FALSE; c) FALSE; d) TRUE. Puntuación: 2/2.
preguntas.criterios: 0,5 puntos por apartado, hasta un máximo de 2 puntos. Para obtener la puntuación de cada apartado, la respuesta debe indicar correctamente TRUE o FALSE y aportar una cita directa del texto que la justifique. No se conceden puntos por indicar únicamente TRUE o FALSE.

a) More than is needed or used.
b) Thrown away because it is no longer wanted or useful.
c) To make a systematic written record of information.
d) To recover something useful from an object that is damaged or no longer needed.

preguntas.enunciado:
Follow the instructions for each item. Answer all the items. (1.5 points)

4.1. Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets. (0.5 points; 0.25 each)
a) By the time the doors open at 10.00 next Saturday, the volunteers ____________________ (complete) the safety checks. Use the future perfect.
b) If a visitor ____________________ (bring) an appliance with exposed wires, the team will refuse to handle it. Use the present simple.

4.2. Complete each sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets. (0.5 points; 0.25 each)
a) Before making a decision, volunteers give visitors practical ____________________ (ADVISE).
b) The civic centre has an ____________________ (ACCESS) ground-floor entrance.

4.3. Join the two sentences using the relative pronoun which. (0.5 points)
The organisers chose the civic centre. It has a ground-floor entrance.
preguntas.solucion:
### 4.1. Formas verbales

**a) By the time the doors open at 10.00 next Saturday, the volunteers _will have completed_ the safety checks.**

- **Comprobación estructural:** la acción de completar los controles habrá terminado antes de un momento futuro concreto. Se usa el futuro perfecto: **will have + participio pasado** (*completed*).

**b) If a visitor _brings_ an appliance with exposed wires, the team will refuse to handle it.**

- **Comprobación estructural:** en una condicional con resultado en futuro (*will refuse*), la cláusula introducida por *if* lleva presente simple. *A visitor* es tercera persona singular, por eso el verbo termina en **-s**.

### 4.2. Formación de palabras

**a) Before making a decision, volunteers give visitors practical _advice_.**

- Se necesita un sustantivo después de *practical*. **Advice** es el sustantivo correspondiente y es incontable; no se escribe *advices* en este uso.

**b) The civic centre has an _accessible_ ground-floor entrance.**

- Se necesita un adjetivo que describa *entrance*. La forma adecuada de *access* es **accessible**.

### 4.3. Oración de relativo

**The organisers chose the civic centre, which has a ground-floor entrance.**

- **Which** introduce una oración de relativo cuyo antecedente es *the civic centre*. La coma es adecuada al añadir la información como descripción adicional.

### Comprobación final

Las formas completan las estructuras exigidas: futuro perfecto, presente simple en la cláusula con *if*, sustantivo, adjetivo y oración de relativo con *which*.
preguntas.resultado: will have completed; brings; advice; accessible; The organisers chose the civic centre, which has a ground-floor entrance.
preguntas.criterios: 4.1a: 0,25 puntos; 4.1b: 0,25 puntos; 4.2a: 0,25 puntos; 4.2b: 0,25 puntos; 4.3: 0,5 puntos por unir correctamente las oraciones con which. Total: 1,5 puntos.

preguntas.enunciado:
Write a composition of 140–160 words on ONE of the following options (a or b). (3 points)

a) Do you think schools should teach students practical skills such as repairing, reusing or sharing everyday objects? Explain your opinion and support it with reasons or examples.

b) Write an email to your school’s environment committee proposing a student-led swap event for books, clothes or other reusable items. Explain how the event could work, what rules would make it fair, and how you would encourage students to take part.

If you choose option b, do not include your name or any identifying information.
preguntas.solucion:
**Opción b**

Subject: Proposal for a Student Swap Event

Dear Environment Committee,

I am writing to propose a student-led swap event at our school. Students could bring books, clothes or other reusable items they no longer need and exchange them for something useful. This would reduce waste, save money and help our school community make more sustainable choices.

To keep it fair, everyone should receive one token for each acceptable item they donate. Items must be clean, safe and in good condition, and each token could be exchanged for one item of similar value. A team of volunteers could check donations, sort them by category and display them clearly. Leftovers could be donated to a local charity.

We could advertise it through classroom announcements, posters and the school website. Holding it during lunch or after classes would make it easy to attend. I hope the committee will support this practical, enjoyable way to reuse resources and bring students together.

Best wishes,

*Extensión: 159 palabras, contando el asunto, el saludo y la despedida.*
